items.title: The Importance of Sight
items.explanation: Helen Keller, who is blind, imagines spending three days to experience the world through sight. She believes that while she can feel the symmetry of a leaf or hear the song of a bird, her eyes are essential for seeing the true self of a person and understanding their emotions like laughter, sorrow, and determination.

items.title: The Three-Day Plan
items.explanation: Helen divides her three days into distinct phases: Day 1 focuses on people's kindness and friendship; Day 2 involves witnessing the miracle of day turning from night with awe; and Day 3 is dedicated to observing the daily lives, progress, and experiences of people in the city.
